checks: Source 8733324562b5a70b gives the same diamond, small diamond, square and ray coefficient. The frozen proof additionally verifies the exact proportional median marginals and gives an equivalent gauge proof of nonconvexity.

The endpoint midpoint is (5/8)A inside the square, so the hull gives the three exact fibers. Independently checked areas 2,4,1/8, total 49/8 and strict-side masses less than 49/16 at the unique median 0.

The independent strict-cross block has raw mass τ=49/528≤1/8. Subtracting the two opposite central blocks leaves the identical nonnegative mass 15/16+τ on each central marginal. Diagonal pairing exhausts it. The normalized weights are τ/m=b/(k+b) and (m−τ)/m=k/(k+b).

Under the determinant-two linear map, each diamond becomes a square with independent coordinates. The one-dimensional convolution plateau and shoulder integrate to one, and the raw density coefficient is (1/8)·2=4ε². Central symmetry, null lines and positive mass in every origin-adjacent open slab give depth 1/2 at zero and strict loss elsewhere.

Along (1,s) in the open sector, the square contributes 1/2 to the integral and the second convolution argument is within its plateau because R(1−s)/(1+s)<ℓ. Direct rational integration gives J=1/8+ε²/24 and c=8ε²J=49/768.

The nonunit radius multiplier is the radial radius divided by the Euclidean length of (1,s), by a change of variable. The gauge restriction is (1+s)/sqrt((1+s)²+c) with strictly negative second derivative. Convexity of the body would imply a convex gauge, so the restricted curvature disproves it.

overlap.comparison: Its radial convexity assumes a convex inverse power of the density. The median-pair density here has no such premise, and the computed gauge defeats convexity.
Its radial representation is for strict inverse-power convex densities; the present example establishes failure of radial convexity for a realizable median target without that regularity.
